finding: Recursive parenthesis peeling in affinity prechecks can overflow a constrained thread stack on a deeply nested in-memory AST.
change: Use iterative parenthesis peeling for no_affinity, text/integer cast literal helpers, literal IN class and scoped CTE column matching; retain original direct-expression recognition and type branches.

red.note: The controlled test constructed 5000 nested AST nodes and called the original no_affinity on a 128 KiB test thread stack; process abort is isolated to the cargo test child. The test was expanded after red.

green.note: Checks positive/negative affinity helper forms and unwraps the deliberately deep AST iteratively before drop.

regression.note: Includes the new helper test; do not add it to 14 as a distinct test.

limits: Controlled synthetic in-memory AST and small thread stack only; not evidence that default or normal SQL causes a natural crash. Actual adapt() preflights SQL bytes, token count and lexical depth; helpers themselves do not establish independent CPU/step limits, and parser, other AST recursion, Linux, real HostLab, A0/A1, full SQL or performance were not qualified. LOWER and general complex BETWEEN repeated evaluation remain unresolved.
